output:
The review is done: I went through all 55 rules and found **10 problems** in `9d62854…HEAD`. The most serious is that this PR changes the Space ID from a number to a UUID in only part of the API, which breaks the other Space routes and several e2e tests.

No tracked files were changed. The checklist was written to the scratchpad (`--out`) instead of `docs/engineering/`, and I did not run tests, tsc or `gh`. I didn't need to look up any past review comments for any rule.

## Findings

**1. The API contract is only half-changed (CHANGE-04, ROUTE-02).** High.
- `src/modules/spaces/routes/spaces.service.ts:108`, `:44` and `:145` now return `id: space.uuid` from `GET /v1/spaces`, `GET /v1/spaces/:id`, `POST /v1/spaces` and `PATCH`.
- But every other Space route still needs a number (`ParseIntPipe` + `RowSchema.shape.id`), for example:
  - `src/modules/spaces/routes/members.controller.ts:96` (and the rest of that file)
  - `src/modules/spaces/routes/address-books.controller.ts:76`
  - `src/modules/spaces/routes/address-book-requests.controller.ts:70`
  - `src/modules/spaces/routes/user-address-book.controller.ts:70`
- The numeric ID is no longer returned anywhere. A client can't call members or address-book routes with any ID the API gives it: the UUID fails `ParseIntPipe` with a 400.
- The change isn't versioned and isn't backward-compatible. Either convert these routes in the same PR or keep accepting both forms for now.

**2. `GET /:id` passes a UUID into a lookup that expects a number (DB-05, TYPE-06).** High.
- `src/modules/spaces/routes/spaces.controller.ts:169-172` passes `id: string` to `getActiveOrInvitedSpace(id: number)` (`spaces.service.ts:54`).
- That value ends up in `{ space: { id: spaceId } }` (`spaces.service.ts:70`), so the query compares an integer column to a UUID.
- This should fail the type check. If it gets through, the route returns 404 or a DB error at runtime.
- The spec calls it with a string too (`spaces.service.spec.ts:538`, `:551`). Unlike update and delete, this route never converts the UUID to the numeric ID.

**3. The entity and the migration describe the unique constraint differently (DB-05).** Medium.
- `src/modules/spaces/datasources/entities/space.entity.db.ts:26` uses `unique: true`. TypeORM turns that into a hash-named UNIQUE *constraint*.
- The migration (`migrations/1779200000000-add-space-uuid.ts:11`) creates a unique *index* named `UQ_spaces_uuid`.
- The next `migration:generate` will see a mismatch and try to change the schema.
- The rest of the repo names these explicitly and matches them to the migration, e.g. `@Unique('UQ_SS_chainId_address_space', …)` in `space-safes.entity.db.ts:17`. The column is also nullable with no index today, so this is the time to settle it.

**4. Existing e2e and integration tests weren't updated (DB-05, TEST-07).** Medium.
- `src/modules/counterfactual-safes/routes/__tests__/space-counterfactual-safes.controller.e2e-spec.ts:117, 165, 190, 224` still cast `body.id as number`.
- Line `:205` requests `/v1/spaces/1/…` and expects 403. It now gets 400 from `ParseUUIDPipe` before the auth check runs.
- `members.controller.e2e-spec.ts:105` and the address-book, user-address-book, space-safes and spaces e2e specs take `body.id` from `POST /v1/spaces` and send it to routes that still expect a number.
- `spaces.repository.integration.spec.ts:218` still expects `{ id, name }`, but `create` now returns `uuid` as well.
- No new test covers the UUID-to-ID lookup or its 404 path.

**5. The same UUID-to-ID helper is copied into three services (REUSE-01, PR-01, MOD-03).** Medium.
- The identical `getNumericId` appears at `spaces.service.ts:124`, `space-safes.service.ts:31` and `space-counterfactual-safes.service.ts:28`.
- To support it, `SpaceCounterfactualSafesService` now also depends on `ISpacesRepository`.
- One repository method (e.g. `ISpacesRepository.findIdByUuidOrFail`) or one shared helper next to `space-assert.utils` would do.

**6. The helper throws, but its name doesn't say so (NAME-01).** Low.
- `getNumericId` throws `NotFoundException` through `findOneOrFail`.
- The repo convention is `*OrFail` for helpers that throw, e.g. `getNumericIdOrFail`.

**7. `update` makes a database call it doesn't need (DB-03).** Low.
- `spaces.service.ts:140-145` looks up the Space again after `update` just to read `uuid`.
- The controller already has the UUID (`spaces.controller.ts:209`) and could pass it through.
- Counting the earlier ID lookup, a PATCH now makes about four DB round-trips.

**8. The controllers now make two service calls per request (ROUTE-01, MOD-06).** Low.
- `spaces.controller.ts:212, 251`, `space-safes.controller.ts:85, 123, 166` and `space-counterfactual-safes.controller.ts:65` each look up the ID, then call the service method.
- That makes the controller orchestrate the use case. Converting the UUID inside the service method (or in a pipe) keeps the controller as a thin HTTP layer.

**9. Existing shared types and schemas aren't reused (TYPE-01, TYPE-04).** Low.
- `space.entity.ts:26` uses `z.string().uuid()` instead of the shared `UuidSchema` in `src/validation/entities/schemas/uuid.schema.ts`.
- `uuid` parameters are typed as a plain `string` rather than `Space['uuid']` or `UUID` (`space-safes.service.ts:31` and the other two copies).
- The Swagger `@ApiParam`/`@ApiProperty` entries don't declare `format: 'uuid'` (e.g. `spaces.controller.ts:150-152`, `create-space.dto.entity.ts:20`).

**10. Formatting and an unrelated change (CHANGE-02).** Low.
- `.gitignore:63-65` adds `/docs`, which has nothing to do with the Space UUID feature.
- `spaces.service.spec.ts:538`, `:551` and `:610` are longer than Prettier's line width, so `yarn format` wasn't run (AGENTS.md requires it before each commit).

## Rules that applied and passed
- **License headers:** every changed source file has the SPDX header.
- **AUTH-05:** membership and admin checks still run before any data is read.
- **SEC-02:** switching to UUIDs for public IDs is what this rule asks for.
- **TEST-01:** the builder uses `faker.string.uuid()`.
- **DB-03 (create):** `create` reads `uuid` from what `save` returns instead of querying again.

Everything else in the checklist didn't apply to this diff.
